Foundations / PAPER 01

The capacity to keep developing

The cornerstone of Omnicorp: improve understanding and agency while preserving purpose, continuity and contact with reality.

WORKING PAPER · DESIGN & ANALYSIS
01

The purpose behind the engines

Omnicorp’s founding purpose is continual development of the organisation’s ability to understand, learn and act. Useful products and physical activity sustain that development and expose it to consequences outside its own reasoning. They are essential sources of resources and feedback, while the ambition extends beyond producing more output.

The transistor offers an analogy for the scale of possibility: a foundational capability can enable uses its first builders cannot fully picture. That is a way to think about uncertainty and preparation, not evidence that AI follows a particular curve or that a singularity has an arrival date.

02

Improvement could belong to a community

One conditional possibility is a community whose members help improve one another. Task performers could generate experience, diagnosticians could identify recurring failures, editors could propose changes and independent evaluators could test the candidates. Integration would be a distinct responsibility rather than an automatic response to a positive report.

This differs from imagining a single model that must understand every task and reliably rewrite itself. Progress might concern tools, communication or the allocation of work before it reaches model capabilities. Direct changes to model weights are a further possibility whose usefulness, reliability and cost would need to be established for a named task.

03

Adaptation is not the same as capability creation

Temporary specialisation could make a general foundation useful in several settings: apply a task-specific change, test it and later restore or switch it. But the ability to edit a model does not establish the ability to find beneficial edits, add missing knowledge or preserve unrelated skills.

Early research on direct weight editing illustrates why that distinction matters. A change may remove an obstruction to an existing capability without creating a new one. Such results can motivate better questions, but they do not demonstrate an indefinitely improving organisation or a reliable community of model editors.

04

Intelligence and the physical world

Improved understanding could help design better machines and infrastructure, which could support further development. This is a possible feedback loop rather than a guarantee of acceleration. Physical systems still require engineering, maintenance, permissions and resources. Some observations and experiments take time that faster design cannot eliminate.

The same practical approach applies to software. A model might generate interfaces and workflows when needed, while records, reliable execution, communication and access control still require dependable implementations. The useful question is which representation performs a job well, rather than whether every operation can be absorbed into a model.

05

What would make development credible?

A meaningful evaluation would define a task, retain an unchanged starting point and test proposed improvements on outcomes that were not used to design them. It would compare simpler alternatives, examine regressions and account for the full effort required to adapt and operate the candidate.

Accepted gains should survive repetition and unfamiliar cases. Parent versions, change history and rollback preserve continuity; independent evaluation prevents a candidate from making its own standard easier. These are future design questions, not a report of a running self-improvement system. The objective and the properties that must endure need explicit human direction.

06

Two turning points, and several kinds of mathematical progress

ChatGPT’s public research preview on 30 November 2022 is our public-encounter milestone. Claude Opus 4.5, released on 24 November 2025, is a developer-work turning point in Omnicorp’s interpretation: delegating substantial work became more compelling to us. That is not a claim that developers first used AI in late 2025; Copilot was already available earlier.

The evidence now includes contest proofs at IMO silver and gold standard, research-level algorithm discovery, a new zeta-function result with external mathematical follow-through, and formalization of Fermat’s Last Theorem. These are different achievements. Formalizing a known proof is not discovering a theorem, and the zeta work did not solve the Riemann hypothesis.

The Observatory attaches sources and limits to each milestone. Its curve is schematic: the date of the present is known, but the height of its dot is an editorial choice with no defined accuracy probability. The numerical forecasts instead concern specific new public records, fixed criteria and deadlines.

THE NEXT QUESTIONS

What remains open.

  • Does an apparent gain persist on unfamiliar tasks?
  • What capabilities and commitments must survive each change?
  • When does the full cost of adaptation outweigh its repeated benefit?
